current_activity: Battle of Toulon: the division liberates the city after heavy fighting
notes: Event date: 27 August 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: Landed in southern France with the army, the division liberates Toulon on 27 August after heavy fighting; the last German command garrison surrenders on 28 August (CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 140). Event support: two source families (Wikipedia and de Lattre's History of the French First Army). Wikipedia, 9th Colonial Infantry Division (France), section History: "On 27 August 1944, the division liberated Toulon after heavy fighting"; de Lattre, The History of the French First Army (1952) p. 92: "On the 24th August the St Catherine fort fell"; p. 76,93: "ending on the 27th August at 23.45 with the unconditional surrender of Admiral Ruhfus". Location: Toulon, Var (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Toulon for the division; de Lattre's notes place it in the Toulon forts on 24-27 August. French follow-up (de Lattre): de Lattre's research notes put the 9th DIC in the Toulon forts from 24 August (St Catherine, p. 92; the Artigues fort and the surrender of the forts, pp. 76, 93) until the unconditional surrender of Admiral Ruhfus at 23.45 on 27 August; a second source family for Toulon on the date, at city level (precision 5 km), so confidence raised from 0.5 to 0.7. The quotes do not name the division; the note line attributes them to the 9th DIC and its 4th RTS.

current_activity: Colmar Pocket: completes the capture of Ensisheim, the original I Corps objective, and drives east
notes: Event date: 6 February 1945 (Wikipedia; CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 551). Event definition: The division attacks Ensisheim, the original objective of the I Corps, on 5 February, completes its capture on 6 February and drives east into the Harth woods. Event support: two source families (Wikipedia and the US Army official history (CMH)). Wikipedia, Colmar Pocket, section Collapse of the Colmar Pocket: "the 9th Colonial Infantry Division attacked Ensisheim, the original corps objective"; "Hirtzfelden was taken by the 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division on 6 February and the 9th Colonial Division completed the capture of Ensisheim and drove east into the Harth Woods"; CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 29 p. 551: "To the south, Bethouart directed his main effort against the last German bridgehead at Chalampe, using the 1st Armored and the 2d Moroccan and 9th Colonial Divisions"; "secure Ensisheim on the 6th". Location: Ensisheim, Haut-Rhin with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Ensisheim for the division; the CMH history dates the capture of Ensisheim to 6 February by the I Corps main effort, which it says used the 1st Armored, 2d Moroccan and 9th Colonial Divisions, without naming the division for the town; two source families for the place and date, the second only for the corps effort, so treated as approximate: 0.7. French follow-up: confidence raised from 0.5 to 0.7 after the CMH history (p. 551) was read.
